system_description.narrative_title: U.S.–Iran conflict driving energy-market and regional diplomacy shocks
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is that U.S.–Iran military confrontation and brinkmanship is the primary driver of swings in global energy markets, regional diplomacy, and shipping risk, with episodic threats and last-minute de‑escalation shaping prices and policy. Viewed as an open system, it admits flows of military actions, diplomatic signals, energy supply disruptions, price signals and investor/firm responses that create reinforcing and balancing feedbacks across states, companies and markets. External perturbations—OPEC+ decisions, Gulf-state diplomacy, shipping incidents and major-power moves (China/Russia/US domestic politics)—continually inject momentum and uncertainty into the system.
system_description.scope: Inside: U.S.–Iran military actions and diplomacy; Gulf states' political and military responses; oil, LNG and shipping through Hormuz/Red Sea; OPEC+ production decisions; oil & fuel price formation; energy firms' production/earnings and investor sentiment; travel/embassy warnings and disruption-related logistics.
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil & gas markets and supply chains
Middle East regional security architecture (Gulf states, Iran, Israel, U.S.)
Global maritime chokepoints and shipping networks (Hormuz, Red Sea)
International financial markets and investor sentiment
evidence_headlines: Embassies warn Americans of travel risk amid signs of possible U.S.-Iran military action in the coming days

variables.name: Military engagement intensity
variables.description: Frequency and average intensity of armed actions and kinetic strikes in the region.

variables.name: Diplomatic signaling rate
variables.description: Rate and polarity (escalatory versus de‑escalatory) of official communications and public diplomatic statements.

variables.name: Maritime transit risk level
variables.description: Likelihood of disruption, interdiction, attack or detention affecting commercial shipping along key sea lanes.

variables.name: Energy supply disruption rate
variables.description: Rate at which physical oil and gas deliveries are interrupted, curtailed or withheld from markets.

variables.name: Crude oil price level
variables.description: Prevailing market price for crude oil per barrel, capturing supply–demand balance and risk premia.

variables.name: Refined fuel price level
variables.description: Market price level for refined petroleum products such as gasoline and diesel used by end consumers.

variables.name: Production quota adjustment rate
variables.description: Frequency and magnitude of coordinated changes in production targets by supply-side actors.

variables.name: Strategic stockpile volume
variables.description: Quantity of liquid fuel reserves available for release to stabilize markets or cover shortfalls.

variables.name: Shipping delay index
variables.description: Average transit time increases and rerouting incidence for maritime cargo caused by regional disruptions.

variables.name: Investor risk appetite
variables.description: Aggregate willingness of investors to hold positions exposed to geopolitical and energy-sector risk.

variables.name: Financial market volatility
variables.description: Degree of short‑term price fluctuation across equity, commodity and currency markets reflecting uncertainty.

variables.name: Freight and logistics cost index
variables.description: Average transport, insurance and rerouting costs for moving energy and related goods through affected corridors.

variables.name: Multilateral diplomatic coordination
variables.description: Degree of coordinated policy alignment, information‑sharing and joint statements among external and regional actors.

variables.name: Sanctions enforcement intensity
variables.description: Strictness and operational reach of economic restriction measures and their implementation efforts.

variables.name: Military force posture level
variables.description: Aggregate readiness, deployed assets and alert status of military forces in and around the region.

variables.name: Upstream investment rate
variables.description: Flow of capital allocated to exploration, development and production capacity in the upstream energy sector.

catalysts.title: Resumption of U.S.–Iran negotiations
catalysts.description: U.S. announcements of resumed talks and cancelled strikes trigger a near‑term diplomatic push to negotiate an off‑ramp.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: Trump says talks to resume/called off strikes; oil falls as diplomacy hopes emerge (Aug 2–4).

catalysts.title: OPEC+ September quota increase
catalysts.description: OPEC+ agreed to a September production hike that will take effect around the start of September, loosening voluntary cuts.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "OPEC+ set for September quota increase"; "OPEC+ members agree to September quota hike."

catalysts.title: Saudi multinational maritime defence coalition
catalysts.description: Saudi plan to build a multinational maritime defence force that could alter regional naval deployments and shipping protection.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Saudi Arabia unveils plans for multinational maritime defence coalition."

catalysts.title: U.S. commander two‑week escalation plan
catalysts.description: Reported U.S. commander plan to escalate strikes over a two‑week window creates a near‑term option to increase kinetic operations.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "The U.S. Commander With a Two-Week Plan to Escalate Strikes in Iran."

catalysts.title: Continued tanker incidents and reroutings
catalysts.description: Ongoing tanker attacks, reported incidents off Oman and reroutings around Africa increase shipping threats and delays near Hormuz/Red Sea.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: UKMTO reports tanker incidents; tankers reroute; "Tankers Are Being Blown Out of the Water."

catalysts.title: Iran–Oman deal to manage Hormuz shipping
catalysts.description: Iran says a deal with Oman to manage shipping through the Strait of Hormuz is close, potentially altering transit protocols and risks.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Iran says deal with Oman to manage shipping through Hormuz is close."

catalysts.title: QatarEnergy buying U.S. LNG cargoes
catalysts.description: QatarEnergy's purchase of dozens of U.S. LNG cargoes to offset Hormuz disruption is an active market mitigation process.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "QatarEnergy buys 33 US LNG cargoes to offset Hormuz disruption."

catalysts.title: Embassy travel warnings and potential evacuations
catalysts.description: Embassies issuing travel warnings increase likelihood of consular evacuations and signal heightened near‑term risk to personnel and commercial activity.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: "Embassies warn Americans of travel risk amid signs of possible U.S.-Iran military action in the coming days."

catalysts.title: Iran threats to strike regional energy fields
catalysts.description: Iran's repeated threats to target energy infrastructure if attacked raise the probability of strikes on energy assets and supply disruptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: "Iran threatens regional energy fields if the U.S. launches fresh attacks" and similar warnings.
